alt.en: A printed page of music, page 302, headed "No. 131. The Crucifixion." in black-letter type: four lines of music for four voices on two staves in G major and 4/4, with the first verse, "Were you there when they crucified my Lord?", under the notes, and verses 2 to 4 printed below.
alt.es: Página impresa de música, la 302, con el encabezado "No. 131. The Crucifixion." en letra gótica: cuatro líneas de música a cuatro voces en dos pentagramas, en Sol mayor y 4/4, con la primera estrofa, "Were you there when they crucified my Lord?", bajo las notas, y las estrofas 2 a 4 impresas debajo.

caption.en: No. 131, "The Crucifixion", on page 302 of the 1892 edition of The Story of the Jubilee Singers: this song's earliest known printing, in four verses, one of them "crowned him with the thorns".
caption.es: El n.º 131, "The Crucifixion", en la página 302 de la edición de 1892 de The Story of the Jubilee Singers: la primera impresión conocida de esta canción, en cuatro estrofas, una de ellas "crowned him with the thorns" (lo coronaron de espinas).

source: J. B. T. Marsh, The Story of the Jubilee Singers, new edition with supplement by F. J. Loudin (Cleveland, Ohio: The Cleveland Printing & Publishing Co., 1892), No. 131, "The Crucifixion", p. 302
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Published Cleveland 1892; J. B. T. Marsh died 1887, F. J. Loudin died 1904, the song is anonymous traditional. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: Princeton Theological Seminary Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed page of music numbered VI, headed "Hymns of the Death of Christ" and "Were You There When They Crucified My Lord?", marked "Adagio con molto espress.", a quarter note equal to 68, and "Solo": the five verses' questions are stacked above the first line, and three systems for four voices on two staves follow, with five verses under the notes.
alt.es: Página impresa de música con el número VI y los encabezados "Hymns of the Death of Christ" y "Were You There When They Crucified My Lord?", con las indicaciones "Adagio con molto espress.", negra igual a 68, y "Solo": las preguntas de las cinco estrofas van apiladas sobre la primera línea, y siguen tres sistemas a cuatro voces en dos pentagramas, con cinco estrofas bajo las notas.

caption.en: Page VI of R. Nathaniel Dett's Religious Folk-Songs of the Negro as Sung at Hampton Institute (1927), which reprints Hampton's 1909 setting and adds the marks "Solo" and "Adagio con molto espress.", at a quarter note to 68: the pace we sing it at.
caption.es: La página VI de Religious Folk-Songs of the Negro as Sung at Hampton Institute (1927), de R. Nathaniel Dett, que reimprime la armonización de Hampton de 1909 y le añade las indicaciones "Solo" y "Adagio con molto espress.", con la negra a 68: el tempo al que la cantamos.

source: R. Nathaniel Dett, ed., Religious Folk-Songs of the Negro as Sung at Hampton Institute (Hampton, Va.: Hampton Institute Press, 1927), Appendix, p. VI, "Were You There When They Crucified My Lord?"
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: "Copyright 1927 by The Hampton Normal and Agricultural Institute": US works published in 1927 entered the public domain on 1 January 2023; Dett died 1943, F. J. Work 1942, so life plus 70 has run out in the EU and Israel. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
